question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 7 & -5 \\ -2 & 9 & -2 & 7 \\ 5 & 3 & 6 & 6 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of ${a}_{41}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the right of ${a}_{41}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 7 & -5 \\ -2 & 9 & -2 & 7 \\ 5 & 3 & 6 & 6 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 4 & 5 \\ 5 & 13 & -9 & 11 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 4 & 5 \\ 5 & 13 & -9 & 11 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+1}|\begin{aligned}7 & -2 & -2 \\ 5 & 4 & 5 \\ 13 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}7 & -2 & -2 \\ 5 & 4 & 5 \\ 13 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
